answer: Could you tell me when the evening Italian course starts?
other_correct: Do you know when the evening Italian course starts?
Could you tell me when the course starts?
When does the evening Italian course start?
Can you tell me when the next Italian course begins?
instruction_problem: Open task: 'some forms are used' is unclear to me; an ordinary direct question (When does the course start?) is also polite and correct, so the intended form (indirect question?) is not forced by the instruction.

answer: Could you tell me when my printer will arrive?
other_correct: Can you tell me when my printer will be delivered?
Could you tell me when I will receive my printer?
Do you know when my printer will arrive?
When will my printer arrive?
Could you tell me why my printer hasn't arrived yet?
Has my order been sent yet?
instruction_problem: Instruction does not force any one form: direct questions, present perfect questions (Has it been sent yet?) are all correct. Unclear what the app checks.

answer: If metal gets hot, it expand.
sense_problem: 'it expand' (missing -s) is a believable learner error.

other_correct: What made that noise in the kitchen?
What made the loud bang in the kitchen?
What made that bang in the kitchen?
What has made that loud bang?
instruction_problem: Situation says 'Ask your flatmate' but the sentence is open: 'What was that?' is excluded only by the word hint. Fine. 'Use What and make' partly gives away the form.

answer: The problem could have been solved much earlier.
other_correct: The problem could have been solved much earlier by someone.
instruction_problem: Does not say 'use the passive' (good), but 'Start with The problem' strongly forces it; acceptable.

answer: would you like to eat something before we leave
other_correct: would you like something to eat before we leave
before we leave, would you like to eat something
before we leave, would you like something to eat
instruction_problem: Cards are all lower case with no capital or punctuation hint; several natural orders exist (something to eat / to eat something; before-clause first).

answer: the bridge was built in 1932 and it is still used today
other_correct: it was built in 1932 and the bridge is still used today
the bridge is still used today and it was built in 1932
in 1932 the bridge was built and it is still used today
the bridge was built in 1932 and is still used today (without it: not possible, card 'it' must be used)
the bridge is still used today and was built in 1932 (no)
instruction_problem: Instruction is bare; no clue whether to start with 'The bridge' or 'It'; several orders are correct.

answer: The winner will be announced on Friday.
other_correct: The winner will be announced on Friday by them.
instruction_problem: Fine; passive forced by 'Start with The winner'.

other_correct: used to read
would read
was reading
had read
instruction_problem: 'was reading' and 'used to read' also fit; 'had read' unlikely. Spelling 'read' is identical to present, so a learner can't be sure of the tense target; only the verb (read) is given.
sense_problem: Past simple intended probably; 'a lot of books ... when he was off work' also supports habitual past (used to / would read).

other_correct: 'd already finished
had finished already
already finished
had already finished
instruction_problem: Gap 'they ___ eating' with 'already / finish' needs 'finished eating' - fine; American 'already finished' is also correct.
